newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco, Spain agree conversion of $50 mln debt.
newsitem.headline: Morocco, Spain agree conversion of $50 mln debt.

text.p: Morocco and Spain on Tuesday signed a deal to convert $50 million of the debt Rabat owes Madrid into cash available for private investments to attract Spanish investors to the North African country.
The deal was signed in Rabat during a ceremony presided over jointly by Moroccan Finance Minister Mohamed Kabbaj and his Spanish counterpart Rodrigo Rato.
"Today's signature is not for protocol purposes...It is a commitment for close cooperation in future, for better integration of Morocco's economy and its development," Rato told reporters.
Spanish companies which are interested in investment projects in Morocco "will totally or partly benefit from funds through the Spanish converted debt," the Spanish minister said.
Moroccan officials said there were an estimated 500 Spanish companies operating in Morocco.
"Spain is a very important partner for us...It is the gateway for our economic and trade policy towards the European Union," Kabbaj said.
Madrid is Morocco's second commercial partner -- after France -- with an estimated $1.0 billion a year, officials said.

"Despite cooperation we did not reach the target set by our two governments, (but) Morocco and Spain are involved in several projects such as electricity interconnetion and Maghreb Europe gas pipeline projects," Kabbaj added.

Moroccan and Spanish officials on Monday inaugurated in the northern Moroccan city of Tangier a $1.4 billion pipeline section linking Algeria's gas field of Hassi R'Mel to southern Spain via northern Morocco.
Morocco's total debt towards Spain is estimated at $1.3 billion, officials said.
Earlier this year, France also accepted the conversion of a Moroccan public debt worth FF 1.5 billion. It had already converted FF 600 million debt to an equity swap.
